text:
incident-bot: PAGING — SLO BREACH detected on /v1/generate (hosted-us-west). p95=1.1s, p99=7.2s (SLO p99 <=5s). Streaming stalls reported; tokenization/preproc tail latency spike. Trace sample: trace/8a3f... Incident id: INC-2150009876
amber: ack @channel I'm oncall. marking triage. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre. Any customer-facing alerts? :rotating_light:
mike: I'm awake, jumping in. amber where're the spans? which route/model?
sophia: quick summary — spike started 2025-11-17T22:33:10Z (aligned with canary of prompt-template-parser v2). Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/2150009876 p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~7.2s, tail (99.9) ~12s. Errors minimal, just high latencies.
eli: looking at preproc pods (preproc-prod-*). CPU top shows tokenizer process at 95% and many syscalls. attaching snippet:
```
2025-11-17T22:33:12Z preproc-3 tokeniser: parsing JSON-mode template took 340ms (norm 5ms)
stack: prompt_parser->json_mode->tokenize_template
```
eli: logs show repeated long waits on parse_tool_schema() on large tool schemas; appears JSON-mode path is quadratic on nested tool schemas.
amber: ok immediate mitigation suggestions? we need to bring p99 <5s asap.
mike: can we disable JSON-mode flag for /v1/generate? that's the risky change from the canary.
eli: yes — feature flag is ff.prompt.json_mode. I can flip it on the control plane. that'll revert to legacy prompt assembly.
eli: also recommend scaling preproc replicas + add a temporary dedicated tokenizer pool:
```
kubectl scale deployment preproc-prod --replicas=6 -n prod
kubectl apply -f preproc-token-pool-temp.yaml
```
sophia: customer impact — initial checks show ~14 affected orgs with traffic routed through prompt-template-parser v2; 3 orgs saw >30% increase in errors/timeouts. cc: @natalie for CS outreach.
natalie: noted. I'll start drafting advisory for those 3 orgs and prepare credit offers if SLAs violated.
amber: mike, please take lead on mitigation. I'm going to hand off on-call to you in 15m unless you need otherwise.
mike: taking over. amber handing to mike at 2025-11-17T22:40:00Z. I'll coordinate infra steps.
eli: flipped ff.prompt.json_mode -> false at 2025-11-17T22:41:05Z. rolling back template-parser canary across canary pools.
infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled preproc-prod from 3 -> 6 replicas (reason: manual scale by eli) at 2025-11-17T22:42:10Z.
eli: after flag flip + scale, p99 dropped to 3.9s within 90s. graphs: https://grafana.redwood/graph/2150009876
sophia: confirmed p99 <5s. monitoring, keep an eye on tail. enabling extra tracing for traces with parse_tool_schema >50ms.
mike: setting temporary rate-limit for large tool-schema requests to reduce load. command:
```
redwood-cli route update /v1/generate --max-tool-schema-size 512KB --burst 50
```
mike: also creating rollback PR to revert prompt-template-parser v2: https://git.redwood/pr/4382
natalie: informed the 3 impacted customers, advising mitigation steps and ETA ~30m. will update on any escalations.
amber: good handoff. mike, please file incident and own postmortem.
mike: will do. initial incident severity: Sev2 (SLO breach, partial customer impact). Timeline & owner: mike (eng-runtime), follow-ups: profiling + algorithmic fix in parser (eli + eng-ml), postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — p99 returned below SLO at 2025-11-17T23:05:20Z. Auto-close window begins. Incident id: INC-2150009876
mike: adding notes: root cause = performance regression in JSON-mode prompt parser with pathological nested tool schemas. Next steps: patch parser to O(n) behavior for nested schemas, add unit tests and a perf guard in rollout.
eli: tagging bench jobs. i'll open a perf PR and add a canary gate on parse latency.
sophia: thanks team. I'll coordinate postmortem and impact scoring.
natalie: I'll send final customer communications after postmortem.
